cards.power: Improvise - Ventricles only catch every 3rd beat.
cards.lore: Decide rate vs. rhythm control, and calculate stroke risk!
cards.gradeReason: Irregularly irregular IS the card. You don't explain AFib, you become it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: punk rabbit chaos. Subject: heart in torn leather jacket, erratic pulse. Mood: chaotic defiance.

cards.power: 2:1 Velvet Rope - Ventricular rate locks at 150.
cards.lore: Vagal maneuvers unmask the flutter waves.
cards.gradeReason: Velvet Rope is inspired, but 300 BPM sawtooth wave needs context to land at table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: butterfly meets disco bouncer. Subject: winged butterfly guarding velvet rope. Mood: exclusive, frenetic.

cards.power: Delta Wave Bypass - Skip AV node delay.
cards.lore: Do NOT give digoxin or AV-blockers if Fibby Fitz is in the club!
cards.gradeReason: Wolf bypassing security is clever, but delta wave is mechanism-speak before you feel the danger.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wolf in suit bypassing velvet rope. Subject: wolf slipping past AV node bouncer. Mood: cunning, dangerous.

cards.power: Total Blackout - Eliminate pulse.
cards.lore: Shock first, ask questions later. No pulse, no negotiation.
cards.gradeReason: STAT: Output ZERO. Total Blackout. This card doesn't explain VF — it IS the code.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon apocalypse rabbit. Subject: flatline character, defibrillator paddles overhead. Mood: zero, terminal, urgent.

cards.power: The Long Wait - Delay, but never drop.
cards.gradeReason: Delay-but-never-drop is a solid role, though benign mechanic needs the table to know what's harmless.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: slow bureaucrat rabbit. Subject: character waiting indefinitely at doorway, PR interval stretching. Mood: tedious, unthreatening.

cards.power: Predictable Fatigue - Progressively longer PR, then drop QRS.
cards.gradeReason: Fatigue that builds then drops is perfectly Wenckebach, but it takes table vocab to perform it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: exhausted marching cartoon. Subject: rabbit stumbling progressively, then collapsing, then restarting. Mood: weary, cyclical.

cards.power: Random Drop - Drop QRS without warning.
cards.gradeReason: Random Drop is strong and playable, but the stakes only land if you know why Mobitz II matters.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: unpredictable hitman. Subject: rabbit dropping cards at random with no warning expression. Mood: sudden, clinical, cold.

cards.power: Severed Comms - Atria and Ventricles march to their own beat.
cards.lore: Bridge therapy required while waiting for the pacemaker!
cards.gradeReason: Marching to your own beat is immediately playable theater. The General commands without needing explanation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: military command rabbit. Subject: two armies marching in opposite directions from one general. Mood: stubborn, disconnected, imperious.

cards.power: ORGANIZED SPEED - WIDE QRS COMPLEX TACHYCARDIA.
cards.lore: Check for pulse! Stable gets meds, unstable gets electricity.
cards.gradeReason: ORGANIZED SPEED is strong, but pulse-check decision tree is instructions before it's a role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: racing sprinter gone wrong. Subject: wide-legged cartoon figure running impossibly fast. Mood: dangerous velocity, unstable urgency.

cards.power: HARD RESET - BRIEFLY FLATLINE THE AV NODE.
cards.lore: Unmask hidden rhythms and terminate SVT.
cards.gradeReason: HARD RESET is a grade-A power name. You don't explain this drug — you deploy it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ninja rabbit with 40-second mission. Subject: assassin pressing pause on a beating heart. Mood: surgical, brief, absolute.

cards.power: CHAOS AGENT - DELAY REPOLARIZATION GLOBALLY.
cards.lore: Watch for thyroid, lung, liver, and blue-gray skin toxicity!
cards.gradeReason: CHAOS AGENT is a knockout power name. Blue-gray skin toxicity in the lore is peak FrizzleBob gold.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: toxic chaos clown rabbit. Subject: blue-tinted character disrupting every organ simultaneously. Mood: chaotic, dangerous, long-lasting.

cards.power: AFFIRM TRIAL - CHOOSE RATE OR RHYTHM.
cards.lore: Rate control is often just as good as rhythm control in AF.
cards.gradeReason: The AFFIRM reference lands for med students, but 'choose rate or rhythm' is a prompt, not a role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: indecisive conductor rabbit. Subject: metronome splitting into two paths labeled RATE and RHYTHM. Mood: deliberate, clinical tension.

cards.power: Demand Ischemia - Attack only during exercise, retreat at rest.
cards.lore: Predictable and reproducible. Fixed stenosis.
cards.gradeReason: Attack-on-exertion is clear role logic, but retreat-at-rest is mechanism before character.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ambush predator cartoon. Subject: rabbit lurking at gym entrance, retreating at couch. Mood: predictable menace, exertion-triggered.

cards.power: Plaque Rupture - Attack without provocation.
cards.lore: Differentiate from NSTEMI by checking Troponin.
cards.gradeReason: Stan attacking unprovoked is a character. The troponin differentiator makes it useful but explanatory.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: unhinged street character. Subject: plaque villain exploding from artery wall with no warning. Mood: volatile, unprovoked, dangerous.

cards.power: Full Occlusion - Elevate ST segments and kill muscle.
cards.lore: Complete occlusion. Time is muscle. Get to the cath lab!
cards.gradeReason: TIME IS MUSCLE is a battle cry. The Plumber sealing a pipe permanently is immediately felt.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: villain plumber rabbit. Subject: plumber cementing coronary pipe shut, clock in background. Mood: catastrophic, time-pressured, final.

cards.power: Leakage Indicator - Detect microscopic cardiac injury.
cards.lore: Sensitive but not specific. Rises in demand ischemia, PE, and renal failure too.
cards.gradeReason: Leakage Indicator is a role you can play. Sensitive-not-specific lore earns its teaching keep.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: forensic detective rabbit. Subject: tiny detective with magnifier at myocyte leak. Mood: precise, over-sensitive, fingerpointing.

cards.power: Vulnerable Plaque - Infiltrate and wait for rupture.
cards.lore: The most dangerous plaques are vulnerable, not the most occlusive.
cards.gradeReason: Infiltrate-and-wait is villain patience at its best. Vulnerable vs occlusive distinction is excellent lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sleeper agent femme fatale rabbit. Subject: lipid character hiding beneath arterial wall, waiting. Mood: patient, dangerous, deceptive.

cards.power: HMG-CoA Block - Upregulate LDL receptors.
cards.lore: Watch the CK levels for myopathy/rhabdo! Give high-intensity post-MI.
cards.gradeReason: Sculptor metaphor lands but HMG-CoA Block is textbook mechanism before it's a character beat.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: artistic sculptor rabbit. Subject: chisel-wielding character reshaping cholesterol plaque into sculpture. Mood: precise, cautionary, disciplined.

cards.power: Irreversible Acetylation - Disable platelet thromboxane A2 forever.
cards.lore: Only a fresh platelet transfusion partially reverses her effect.
cards.gradeReason: Irreversible Acetylation is a power name med students feel, but it needs context to click at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ancient elder rabbit. Subject: old wizard permanently marking platelets with acetyl stamp. Mood: permanent, ancient, unstoppable.

cards.power: ADP Blockade - Prevent platelet aggregation.
cards.lore: Combines with Aspirin for DAPT after stent placement.
cards.gradeReason: Ticky is charming but ADP Blockade reads like a biochem slide before it becomes a character.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sidekick rabbit. Subject: small character blocking platelet handshake between two cells. Mood: prevention, teamwork, junior partner.

cards.power: Venodilation - Relieve angina and pulmonary edema.
cards.lore: Fatal hypotension if combined with PDE5 inhibitors! Avoid in RV infarcts.
cards.gradeReason: Negotiator who relieves angina AND could kill you with Viagra is pure G1 character energy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: smooth-talking diplomat rabbit. Subject: nitro character opening veins like negotiations at table. Mood: diplomatic, precariously useful.

cards.power: Cardioprotection - Reduce oxygen demand and block remodeling.
cards.lore: Contraindicated acutely in decompensated HF or severe block.
cards.gradeReason: Beta the Bouncer is immediately embodied. Cardioprotection as bouncer duty is instantly playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: nightclub bouncer rabbit. Subject: burly beta-blocker guarding heart entrance, slowing admission. Mood: protective, gate-controlling, selective.

cards.power: Scaffold - Hold open the culprit lesion.
cards.lore: Drug-eluting stents (DES) prevent restenosis but need longer DAPT.
cards.gradeReason: Scaffold is a playable construction role, but SYNTAX score and DES nuance push this toward a lecture.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: engineer rabbit. Subject: architect rabbit inserting wire scaffold into blocked pipe. Mood: technical, precise, interventional.

cards.power: New Plumbing - Bypass the obstruction entirely.
cards.lore: Preferred for left main disease, 3-vessel disease, and complex diabetics.
cards.gradeReason: New Plumbing as a card power is beautifully literal. Left main and 3-vessel criteria make this table-essential.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: construction worker rabbit. Subject: plumber routing new pipe around blocked artery segment. Mood: decisive, surgical, infrastructural.

cards.power: Weak Squeeze - Drop output, pool fluid.
cards.lore: Classify functional severity using the NYHA class.
cards.gradeReason: Weak Squeeze is a physical role you can play. NYHA classifying is useful but explanatory lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: exhausted laborer rabbit. Subject: deflated cartoon heart character barely pumping, fluid pooling around feet. Mood: depleted, struggling.

cards.power: Flash Flood the Alveoli - Crackles, orthopnea, fluid overload.
cards.lore: Differentiate cardiac from pulmonary dyspnea using BNP/NT-proBNP.
cards.gradeReason: Eddie flooding the lungs is immediately tactile. BNP differentiation is excellent diagnostic lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: flooding cartoon. Subject: water-logged rabbit overflowing lungs with fluid, gasping upright. Mood: drowning, breathless, orthopneic.

cards.power: Vasodilation - Drop afterload, stop remodeling.
cards.lore: Causes a bradykinin-mediated dry cough. Switch to ARB if intolerable!
cards.gradeReason: Afterload architect is a serviceable role. Dry cough lore is the memorable pearl that saves the card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: architect-builder rabbit. Subject: ACE inhibitor character redesigning hypertrophied walls. Mood: remodeling, constructive, slightly annoying (cough).

cards.power: Dual Strike - Block AT1 receptor AND boost natriuretic peptides.
cards.lore: Wait 36 hours after stopping ACE before starting Arnie (Angioedema risk)!
cards.gradeReason: Dual Strike is a strong power. The 36-hour angioedema window is a table-critical pearl.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dual-wielding fighter rabbit. Subject: character striking from two angles simultaneously in heart diagram. Mood: superior, precision-timed, upgraded.

cards.power: Anti-Fibrotic - Block the mineralocorticoid receptor.
cards.lore: Reduces mortality in severe HFrEF, but watch for hyperkalemia and gynecomastia.
cards.gradeReason: Aldo the Antagonist is a great villain-role name. Mineralocorticoid receptor mechanism needs framing at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: antagonist villain rabbit. Subject: character opposing aldosterone fibrosis with anti-fibrotic shield. Mood: opposed, pharmacological, bodyguard energy.

cards.power: Osmotic Diuresis - Block glucose reabsorption in the kidney.
cards.lore: The diabetes drug that became a heart failure mortality-reducing hero!
cards.gradeReason: The diabetes-drug-turned-hero is the lore saving this card. Osmotic Diuresis is dry mechanism before that.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: unexpected hero rabbit. Subject: diabetic drug character arriving in heart ward as surprise savior. Mood: redemptive, crossover, underdog triumph.

cards.power: Inotropic Boost - Inhibit Na/K-ATPase to increase intracellular Calcium.
cards.lore: Hypokalemia dramatically increases the risk of Diggy toxicity!
cards.gradeReason: Narrow therapeutic index is a playable danger. Na/K-ATPase mechanism buries the character before it starts.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tightrope-walking rabbit. Subject: digoxin character balancing on narrow safe margin, potassium below. Mood: precarious, antique, toxic threshold.

cards.power: Flash Flood - Massive diuresis via ascending loop of Henle.
cards.lore: The front-line decongestive in acute HF. Watch for ototoxicity at high IV doses.
cards.gradeReason: Flash Flood is an excellent power. Lou is a good name. Ototoxicity lore earns its keep.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: water park operator rabbit. Subject: loop diuretic character opening massive flood gates in kidney tubule. Mood: powerful, fast, noisy.

cards.power: Dilate & Thin - Change ventricular geometry over time.
cards.lore: ACEi, Beta-Blockers, and Aldo-antagonists starve this monster.
cards.gradeReason: Monster that dilates and thins is immediately felt. Starving it with three drugs is a boss-fight payoff.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: slowly expanding monster rabbit. Subject: heart-shaped monster stretching walls thin over time. Mood: creeping threat, geometric horror.

cards.power: Silent Guardian - Deliver synchronized shock for VT, unsync for VF.
cards.lore: Primary prevention of sudden cardiac death in optimized HFrEF.
cards.gradeReason: Silent Guardian is good but the sync/unsync distinction makes it feel like a manual before a character.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: armored watchman rabbit. Subject: ICD device character standing guard inside chest cavity, waiting. Mood: vigilant, silent, ready.

cards.power: Resynchronization - Force Left and Right ventricles to squeeze together.
cards.lore: Indicated specifically for HFrEF patients with LBBB morphology.
cards.gradeReason: Squeeze-together is a physical act you can embody. LBBB morphology criteria narrows the audience who gets it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: choreographer rabbit. Subject: two ventricle characters forced to dance in sync by conductor. Mood: synchronized, rhythmic, therapeutic.

cards.power: New Engine - Swap Franko out completely.
cards.lore: Contraindicated by active infection, malignancy, or severe fixed pulmonary HTN.
cards.gradeReason: New Engine replacing Franko is an elegant callback payoff. Passport metaphor works as last resort.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: new arrival at immigration rabbit. Subject: fresh heart character presenting passport at chest door. Mood: last resort, new beginning, gatekept.

cards.power: Silent Killer - Sustain high pressure indefinitely.
cards.lore: Urgency = no organ damage (oral meds). Emergency = organ damage (IV meds).
cards.gradeReason: Silent Killer is a known trope, and urgency/emergency distinction is excellent clinical lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: invisible threat rabbit. Subject: pressure gauge character slowly redlining with no symptoms visible. Mood: silent menace, insidious, systemic.

cards.power: Constrict & Retain - Spike BP and hoard volume.
cards.lore: Feeds on low renal perfusion and sympathetic activation.
cards.gradeReason: Constrict-and-hoard is a playable villain role. Feeding on low perfusion makes the loop visceral and clear.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: hoarding villain rabbit. Subject: RAAS character squeezing arteries while stockpiling fluid. Mood: constricting, greedy, feedback-loop driven.

cards.power: Smooth Muscle Relax - Block L-type calcium channels.
cards.lore: Dihydropyridines (amlodipine) cause edema. Verapamil slows the AV node and causes constipation.
cards.gradeReason: L-type calcium channel blocking is pure mechanism. Cal needs a role, not a pharmacology classification.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: relaxed bouncer rabbit. Subject: character blocking calcium from entering smooth muscle cell doors. Mood: relaxed, selectively blocking, calm.

cards.power: Volume Drop - Block NaCl cotransport.
cards.lore: First-line agent! Causes hypokalemia, hyponatremia, and hyperuricemia (watch for gout).
cards.gradeReason: NaCl cotransport blocking is a mechanism, not a role. ALLHAT Champion badge isn't enough to rescue this.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bureaucratic filter rabbit. Subject: tubule character blocking salt passage with stamp. Mood: procedural, clinical, unexciting.

cards.power: Arterial Drop - Sudden Peripheral vasodilation.
cards.lore: Great for BPH, but causes brutal first-dose orthostatic hypotension!
cards.gradeReason: First-dose faceplant is an instantly performable clinical disaster. Aloha Annie greets you with a fall.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cheerful face-planting rabbit. Subject: character waving aloha then immediately dropping from vasodilation. Mood: cheerfully dangerous, orthostatic.

cards.power: Systemic Storm - HTN + Proteinuria + End-organ failure.
cards.lore: Mag sulfate is for seizures, NOT BP control. Give Labetalol or Nifedipine. Cure = Delivery.
cards.gradeReason: Systemic Storm is evocative. Mag-not-for-BP is a high-yield lore gem. Cure = Delivery lands perfectly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pregnant storm character rabbit. Subject: systemic storm consuming organs with proteinuria rain. Mood: emergency, maternal crisis, time-sensitive.

cards.power: Instant Drop - Second-by-second BP control.
cards.lore: Perfect for emergencies, but prolonged use risks Cyanide Toxicity! Monitor a-line.
cards.gradeReason: Second-by-second BP control is a high-stakes real-time role. Cyanide toxicity is the villain in the lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: precision speed rider rabbit. Subject: motorcycle character controlling blood pressure gauge second-by-second. Mood: surgical speed, urgent, poisonous if slow.

cards.power: Catecholamine Dump - Episodic HTN, headache, diaphoresis.
cards.lore: MUST give Alpha-blocker BEFORE Beta-blocker, or risk a lethal hypertensive crisis!
cards.gradeReason: Hidden Villain who dumps catecholamines is pure theater. Alpha-before-Beta lore is a life-or-death performance cue.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: shadow villain rabbit. Subject: pheochromocytoma villain unmasking with catecholamine explosion. Mood: episodic terror, hidden menace, lethal sequence.

cards.power: Tearing Pain - Propagate the flap down the aorta.
cards.lore: Type A (Ascending) = Surgical Emergency. Type B (Descending) = Medical management (HR/BP control).
cards.gradeReason: Tearing Pain propagating a flap is viscerally felt. Type A vs B decision tree is essential table logic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ripping action villain rabbit. Subject: aorta character splitting with dramatic tear from chest to abdomen. Mood: tearing, catastrophic, directional emergency.

cards.power: Hidden Cause - Sleep apnea, Renal artery stenosis, Aldosteronism.
cards.lore: Suspect if BP is refractory to 3 agents or starts before age 50!
cards.gradeReason: Listing three suspects is a diagnosis checklist, not a character. The role is underdeveloped despite the tension.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: detective lineup rabbit. Subject: three suspect rabbits in police lineup — apnea, renal stenosis, aldosteronism. Mood: investigative, hidden, clinical.

cards.power: Fixed Outflow - Restrict LV emptying.
cards.lore: Symptoms = Angina, Syncope, Dyspnea (SAD). Once symptomatic, survival drops fast! (TAVR vs SAVR).
cards.gradeReason: SAD mnemonic is useful but the card lists symptoms rather than inviting you to embody outflow obstruction.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: immovable obstacle rabbit. Subject: armored Arnie blocking the LV outflow tract. Mood: immovable, narrowing, ominous symptom clock.

cards.power: Volume Overload - Flood the left atrium and lungs.
cards.lore: Acute MR (papillary rupture) is a shock emergency. Chronic MR is compensated for years.
cards.gradeReason: Flooding atrium and lungs is a physical act. Acute vs chronic split in lore is clean clinical teaching.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: flooding character rabbit. Subject: mitral valve open backwards, blood flooding into atrium. Mood: leaking, overloading, acute vs chronic split.

cards.power: Atrial Stretch - Dilation, AFib, and Pulmonary HTN.
cards.lore: Almost always rheumatic in origin. Listen for the opening snap!
cards.gradeReason: Atrial Stretch is a mechanism before a role. Rheumatic origin + opening snap reads like a physical exam note.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: narrowing doorway rabbit. Subject: mitral valve tightening with stretched atrium behind it. Mood: rheumatic, progressive, historical constraint.

cards.power: Friction Rub - Positional sharp chest pain.
cards.lore: If fluid accumulates fast, Tamponade hits (Beck's Triad, Pulsus Paradoxus). Time for pericardiocentesis!
cards.gradeReason: Friction Rub as a power name is instant. Beck's Triad and Pulsus Paradoxus as lore payoff is stellar.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: armored knight rabbit. Subject: pericardial knight with shield generating friction sparks. Mood: sharp, positional, escalating toward tamponade.

cards.power: RV Strain - Cor Pulmonale and right heart failure.
cards.lore: Group 1 gets advanced pulmonary vasodilators, Groups 2-5 need their root cause fixed!
cards.gradeReason: Group classification is a WHO flowchart, not a role. RV Strain is physical but the card stays clinical.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: straining weight-lifter rabbit. Subject: right ventricle character buckling under high pulmonary pressure. Mood: strained, isolated, group-dependent.

cards.power: Delivery Boy - Drop lipid packages into the vascular intima.
cards.lore: Statins first. If LDL targets aren't met in high-risk patients, deploy PCSK9 inhibitors!
cards.gradeReason: Delivery Boy as a power is slightly weak but functional. PCSK9 escalation lore is solid teaching.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: delivery worker rabbit. Subject: LDL character in delivery uniform dropping lipid boxes into arterial walls. Mood: mundane menace, accumulating damage.

cards.power: Antithrombin III Buff - Inhibit Thrombin and Factor Xa.
cards.lore: Reversible with protamine. LMWH (enoxaparin) requires less monitoring but renally cleared!
cards.gradeReason: Antithrombin III Buff is mechanistic game language that lands for RPG-literate med students.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: medieval buffer tank rabbit. Subject: heparin character boosting antithrombin shield against clot army. Mood: protective, old-school, reversible.

cards.power: Direct Blockade - Predictable kinetics, no INR checks.
cards.lore: Replaced warfarin for most AFib/VTE. Reverse dabigatran with idarucizumab, Xa with andexanet alfa.
cards.gradeReason: Squad concept works but Direct Blockade is mechanism before character. Reversal agents in lore are table gold.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: modern squad rabbit. Subject: NOAC team replacing old warfarin guard with efficient direct blockers. Mood: upgraded, predictable, reversal-ready.

cards.power: Pimping - Demand a fully integrated clinical regimen.
cards.lore: 68yo diabetic, AFib, EF 32%. Build the optimal regimen, spot the interactions, set the targets!
cards.gradeReason: PIMPING as a power name is perfect med school theater. The case is a capstone synthesis prompt.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: imposing professor rabbit. Subject: attending rabbit grilling student with 68yo diabetic AFib HF case. Mood: demanding, integrative, academic fire.

cards.power: Story trumps Lists - Discard rote memorization.
cards.lore: The science is real, the absurdity makes it permanent. You remember stories, not spreadsheets.
cards.gradeReason: Meta-card is the thesis statement of the entire deck. Story-over-lists IS the performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: meta-manifesto rabbit. Subject: FrizzleBob holding golden stethoscope, lists of drugs burning beneath. Mood: triumphant, anti-memorization, creed.

verdict: MedKayfab Cardiology ADD rolls 56 deep across arrhythmias, ACS, heart failure, hypertension, valves, and anticoagulation — comprehensive spine, no obvious gaps. Pheo the Hidden Villain, Ami the Pamiodar, The General, and FrizzleBob's Golden Stethoscope are hall-of-famers. Liability is a cluster of mechanism-heavy G3s in the middle tier: Cal the Calcium Blocker, Distal Convoluted, Secondary Suspects, and Patrice the PAH explain rather than invite. Critical QA note: some cards label the teaching layer CORE, others LORE — this inconsistency must be standardized before Gumroad. Table-ready Y.
blurb: For med students who'd rather perform the RAAS than memorize it — 56 cardiology characters covering arrhythmias, ACS, heart failure, hypertension, and valves through role-play and absurdist card battles.
